The tool journey, step by step#

This is the loop the alpha supports end to end for a tool, with each step as a page action. caliber/caliber-ui/e2e/tool-journey.spec.ts drives it on the shipped defaults (it saves the fixtures and creates the workflow through the API, the endpoints the page's editors save to).

#StepIn the page (Tools)What you should see
1RegisterRegister Tool, then the wizard: name, module, callable, input schemathe tool's workspace (/tools?tool=TL-…, an address a reload keeps)
2Run itSandbox, then Test Run, with a JSON object as input (anything else is refused with a message, not run)the tool's output, produced by the sandbox
3Save fixturesopen the tool, Fixtures: add cases with an input and an assertionthe cases are saved against the tool
4CalibrateFixtures: Run calibration"Pass rate 100% — 2/2 passed", or which cases failed
5Pin a baselineTest Runs: Set as baseline on a run (a run is saved when you invoke the tool on Sandbox or run the suite on Hardening)the run carries a Baseline marker, and later runs are compared to it
6Use it in a workflowreference the tool from an agent node in a workflow versionthe workflow appears under Publish, Where used
7Make a new versionPublish, Version history, New version (admins): the wizard opens on the tool with its name fixed and the version one on; change what differs and registerthe new version's own workspace; the history lists both versions, and you can promote or roll back between them

Two things about the Tools list. A fresh install lists sixteen tools that CALIBER seeded itself, and each is labelled Built-in, so you can tell them from the ones an admin registered. Four of them are the agent-memory tools (memory_search, memory_list, list_entities, memory_add). While agent memory is off (CALIBER_MEMORY_ENABLED is not true) they are labelled Unavailable, with the reason on the row, because wiring one into a workflow would only make it return an error at run time.

Who is trusted to write tools#

Read this before you let anyone register a tool.

  • Tool authors are trusted. A registered tool is code, imported from a Python module and called. Only a global admin can register, change or archive a tool, and that is the whole of the trust model: CALIBER does not defend itself against an admin who registers a malicious tool.
  • The sandbox is a process boundary, not a container. By default each call runs in a separate Python interpreter with an empty environment, a private working directory, resource limits and a wall-clock deadline that kills the process group. It is not a container, virtual machine or seccomp boundary: the child keeps ambient filesystem and network access on the host. That is appropriate for tool authors you trust and is not isolation from ones you do not. Set CALIBER_TOOL_SANDBOX_BACKEND to a backend you provide if you need OS-enforced isolation. Without one, promoting a workflow version that uses registered tools to a production-class alias is refused: CALIBER_TOOL_SANDBOX_REQUIRE_EXTERNAL_ISOLATION_FOR_ENVIRONMENT_CLASSES defaults to production (set it empty to turn the gate off), and an alias whose name is not recognised as staging or development counts as production.
  • Restrict which modules a tool may come from. CALIBER_REGISTERED_TOOL_MODULE_ALLOWLIST is a comma-separated list of module prefixes, for example caliber.*,mycompany.tools.*. It ships empty, which means any importable module may be registered, and /readiness reports that as "registered tool modules are unrestricted" (a check that is not required, so it never fails readiness). Set it for anything beyond a local trial.
  • Inside a project, roles apply on top of that. Registering, changing or archiving a tool needs caliber.admin and, for a project tool, editor or owner; saving fixtures needs editor or owner. Running a tool, starting a calibration, recording a test run and setting a baseline need reviewer, editor or owner, and each of those also needs caliber.operator. Reading needs only membership. A member whose role is too weak gets 403 and a person outside the project gets 404. See Auth and project scoping.
  • Side effects need approval. A tool that writes or acts on an external system is registered with approval required, and the sandbox mocks it in preview runs.
  • Workflows add a second boundary of the same kind. A python_code node is authorable by operators. Preview refuses it and a published run blocks import, but that is containment, not isolation.

1. What tools are for in CALIBER#

Tools are versioned callable assets. They are not just snippets attached to a prompt. CALIBER tracks their contract, tests, and execution boundaries because they may touch real external systems.
